gaps.sentence: Endangered plants ___ (not pick) anywhere in the reserve.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive of prohibition: must not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: Every complaint ___ (investigate) since the new ombudsman took over.
gaps.explanation: 'Every complaint' is singular, so present perfect passive: has been + investigated.

gaps.sentence: The house looked deserted; it ___ (empty) years earlier.
gaps.hint: past event before another past point
gaps.explanation: 'Years earlier' is before the past reference point, so past perfect passive: had been + emptied.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
gaps.explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

gaps.sentence: The new policy ___ (CRITICISE) sharply since it was announced.
gaps.explanation: 'Since' + continuing result: present perfect passive has been criticised.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ in the twelfth century.
gaps.explanation: A completed past date takes the past simple passive.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).
